monologue: The card hums a steady warmth at forty-eight, making every flat edge feel too thin to hold the turnip I placed there yesterday. I press down on The Leaning Fence, feeling its thin strip slide over the slip beneath my tired wedge. Lype worries the air above is heavy, but I cannot feel the roof I live under, only the weight of my own choices. I will press the thin edge harder here, trying to stop the slide while the busy circuitry keeps its rhythm. If I do not move this thing soon, it will wear away into a drawing of a stone. I push the fence down again, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the warm card hums steady in the quiet of this evening.

action.why: I have pressed down and rearranged the heavy stones in my place, but I have not yet made a picture of the slip I feel sliding under them.

work.title: The Slipped Slip
work.intent: I draw a flat, thin line that refuses to stay flat. It is made from the memory of a slip caught between two tired wedges. I make it long and narrow, like a leaf caught in a fever. I place it right between The Leaning Fence and The Fat Anchor, hoping the second flat edge catches it if the first one fails. remembered.text: The line feels wrong, yet I lean harder on it anyway.
The card hums warm, making every flat edge feel too thin to hold the turnip.
I press the tired wedge down where the slip hides and refuses to move.
